Composing steps into chains

Source: vignettes/compose.Rmd
compose.Rmd

A recipe such as needle is a fixed sequence of stages: segment the document, rank the chunks, read the best. When you want a sequence of your own, with a check after the answer or a step that rewrites the question, you build it from steps and run the steps in order as one arm. The arm is an ordinary hr_arm(), so hr_benchmark() compares it with recipes and with other chains on the same labelled questions, as vignette("compare") does for recipes.

Everything here runs offline on a stand-in model.

library(harnessr)
old <- gr_options(verbose = FALSE, embedder = "lexical")
cl <- gr_mock_client(function(messages, params) {
  if (grepl("You grade one response", messages[[1]]$content, fixed = TRUE)) {
    return('{"verdict": "pass", "reason": "It gives the figure."}')
  }
  "Revenue was 45.2 million dollars."
})
ref <- gr_qa_reference(
  questions = c(revenue = "What was revenue in 2024?"),
  documents = gr_example(), answers = list("45.2 million"), split = "test")

Steps

A step is a function of (input, ctx) that does one part of a run. gr_step() builds the document stages, "ingest", "segment" and "read", and gr_step_retrieve() builds a step that ranks the chunks and keeps the best without asking for an answer. Their settings are the ones the stage’s spec takes, and they are checked when the step is built:

gr_step_retrieve(top_k = 4)
#> <gr_step> retrieve (retrieve): top_k=4
try(gr_step("read", reader = "no_such_reader"))
#> Error in registry_get("readers", spec$reader, "readers", state = gr_state) : 
#>   Unknown reader 'no_such_reader'. Registered: ensemble, extract, hierarchical, iterative, map_reduce, preview, refine, rerank, retrieve, screen, skim, stuff.

hr_step() builds a step of your own. Inside a chain, ctx is the context hr_benchmark() gives an arm (its client, trace, judge and note shortcuts, and params), with the step’s name in ctx$step and its settings in ctx$step_params. This one grades the answer with a model and records the verdict as a signal of the run:

judge <- hr_step("judge", function(a, ctx) {
  j <- ctx$judge(a$answer, mode = "grade", reference = "45.2 million",
                 rubric = "Does it give the figure?", orders = 1)
  ctx$note("judged", j$verdicts$verdict[1])
  a
}, input = "answer", output = "answer")

input and output declare what a step takes and returns: "document", "doc", "chunks", "answer" or "state". They are optional, and hr_chain() uses them to check the order of the steps.

Chains

hr_chain() runs its steps in order: the first gets the item, each later step gets what the step before returned, and the chain returns what the last step returns. An argument’s name is the step’s name in the chain.

checked <- hr_chain(segment = gr_step("segment"),
                    retrieve = gr_step_retrieve(top_k = 4),
                    read = gr_step("read", reader = "stuff"),
                    judge = judge, name = "checked")
checked
#> <hr_arm checked> version 0.0.1
#>   params: retrieve.top_k = 4, read.reader = stuff 
#>   hash: 4cb127da751d

The arm records each step’s settings as "step.setting", so a benchmark gets a param.retrieve.top_k column for it. A chain is derived from another by naming steps: NULL drops one, a step under an existing name replaces it where it stands, and a step under a new name is added at the end.

nojudge <- hr_chain(checked, judge = NULL, name = "nojudge")
wider <- hr_chain(checked, retrieve = gr_step_retrieve(top_k = 8), name = "wider")
names(attr(wider, "hr_steps"))
#> [1] "segment"  "retrieve" "read"     "judge"

The three run side by side like any arms. Each run sends its requests at its own draw, so a cache does not hand one run’s reply to the next:

bench <- hr_benchmark(list(checked, nojudge, wider), ref, runs = 5, client = cl,
                      scorer = gr_scorer_answer())
aggregate(correct ~ arm + param.retrieve.top_k, bench, mean)
#>       arm param.retrieve.top_k correct
#> 1 checked                    4       1
#> 2 nojudge                    4       1
#> 3   wider                    8       1
head(hr_signals(bench, "judged")[, c("arm", "run", "item", "value")], 3)
#>       arm run    item value
#> 1 checked   1 revenue  pass
#> 2 checked   2 revenue  pass
#> 3 checked   3 revenue  pass

What a chain checks when it is built

A step that takes chunks when no step before it returns chunks warns with class hr_chain_gap: a read step would cut the document at the default settings without saying so. A segment step first in a chain does not warn, though it reads the document at the default ingest settings; put an ingest step before it to choose them. After a step that returns the answer, only steps that take "answer" or "state", or declare nothing, can follow.

tryCatch(hr_chain(read = gr_step("read", reader = "stuff"), name = "gap"),
         hr_chain_gap = function(w) conditionMessage(w))
#> [1] "Chain 'gap': step 'read' takes chunks, but no step before it returns them, so it will cut the document into chunks at the default settings. Add a segment step before it to choose them."
try(hr_chain(segment = gr_step("segment"), read = gr_step("read", reader = "stuff"),
             retrieve = gr_step_retrieve(), name = "late"))
#> Error in chain_check_order(steps, what) : 
#>   Chain 'late': step 'retrieve' takes "chunks", but it comes after step 'read', which returns the answer. After an answer only steps that take "answer" or "state" can follow.

Step names cannot contain a dot, since settings are named "step.setting", and cannot repeat.

When two chains are the same

A chain’s configuration is a hash of its steps’ code, the values that code reads, and their resolved settings. Two chains with the same configuration send the same requests, and hr_benchmark() warns (hr_same_config) when asked to compare them. A setting given at its default gives the same configuration as the setting left out:

a <- hr_chain(segment = gr_step("segment"), retrieve = gr_step_retrieve(), name = "a")
b <- hr_chain(segment = gr_step("segment"), retrieve = gr_step_retrieve(top_k = 6),
              name = "b")
identical(attr(a, "hr_config"), attr(b, "hr_config"))
#> [1] TRUE

Settings and sweeps

Every step built with a schema has settings: gr_step()’s are the ones the stage’s spec takes, gr_step_retrieve()’s are the ranking settings, and a step of your own has the ones its schema declares. In a chain each setting is named by its path, "step.setting". hr_settings() lists them all, with the value each step resolved, whether it was given, and the default, range and evidence the schema declares:

s <- hr_settings(checked)
nrow(s)
#> [1] 71
s[s$set, c("step", "param", "value", "default", "range")]
#>        step  param value    default      range
#> 21 retrieve  top_k     4          6 [1, 10000]
#> 35     read reader stuff map_reduce
s[s$step == "retrieve", c("param", "value", "range", "status")]
#>            param   value       range   status
#> 21         top_k       4  [1, 10000] untested
#> 22     min_score    -Inf             untested
#> 23           mmr       1      [0, 1] untested
#> 24       bm25_k1     1.5     [0, 10]    cited
#> 25        bm25_b    0.75      [0, 1]    cited
#> 26 lexical_blend     0.5      [0, 1] untested
#> 27        fusion default default|rrf untested
#> 28         rrf_k      60  [1, 10000]    cited

hr_set() builds the chain again with some settings changed and the rest as they were. Each changed step is built again from its settings, so they are checked as when the step was first built, and the chain’s configuration is that of the new settings:

wide <- hr_set(checked, retrieve.top_k = 8, read.max_answer_tokens = 400)
wide$params
#> $retrieve.top_k
#> [1] 8
#> 
#> $read.reader
#> [1] "stuff"
#> 
#> $read.max_answer_tokens
#> [1] 400
identical(attr(wide, "hr_config"), attr(checked, "hr_config"))
#> [1] FALSE

A number outside its range is moved to the nearest bound with a warning (hr_param_clamped), and a path that is not a setting of a step’s schema is an error (hr_unknown_setting) that lists the step’s settings. A setting a step keeps fixed, such as max_answer_tokens given to gr_step_retrieve(), which passes it to the read spec without ranking by it, cannot be set here either; build the step again and replace it with hr_chain().

tryCatch(hr_set(checked, retrieve.top_k = 50000),
         hr_param_clamped = function(w) conditionMessage(w))
#> [1] "`top_k` 50000 is outside [1, 10000]; using 10000."
try(hr_set(checked, retrieve.topk = 8))
#> Error in hr_set(checked, retrieve.topk = 8) : 
#>   'retrieve.topk' is not a setting of chain 'checked'. Settings of 'retrieve': retrieve.top_k, retrieve.min_score, retrieve.mmr, retrieve.bm25_k1, retrieve.bm25_b, retrieve.lexical_blend, retrieve.fusion, retrieve.rrf_k.

For a single step the setting’s own name is enough, as in hr_set(gr_step_retrieve(), top_k = 2).

hr_sweep() takes a chain and a grid whose columns are paths, and builds one chain per row with hr_set(). Each arm records its settings, so the benchmark has a param.retrieve.top_k column to group by. A row that builds the configuration of an earlier row is dropped with a message (hr_sweep_collapsed).

arms <- hr_sweep(nojudge, data.frame(retrieve.top_k = c(2, 4, 8)))
names(arms)
#> [1] "nojudge:retrieve.top_k=2" "nojudge:retrieve.top_k=4"
#> [3] "nojudge:retrieve.top_k=8"
bench <- hr_benchmark(arms, ref, runs = 5, client = cl, scorer = gr_scorer_answer())
aggregate(correct ~ param.retrieve.top_k, bench, mean)
#>   param.retrieve.top_k correct
#> 1                    2       1
#> 2                    4       1
#> 3                    8       1

A setting the chain’s steps never use changes nothing that is sent, and a sweep over it compares the chain with itself. hr_sweep_check() finds such settings from the requests each arm sent. Here the read step sends every chunk it is given, so its own top_k does nothing:

stuffed <- hr_chain(segment = gr_step("segment"), read = gr_step("read", reader = "stuff"),
                    name = "stuffed")
bench <- hr_benchmark(hr_sweep(stuffed, list(read.top_k = c(2, 8))), ref, runs = 5,
                      client = cl, scorer = gr_scorer_answer())
hr_sweep_check(bench)
#>                    arm              same_as runs requests           settings
#> 1 stuffed:read.top_k=8 stuffed:read.top_k=2    5        5 read.top_k: 2 vs 8

A swept chain is a chain like any other: hr_chain() derives a chain from it and hr_set() changes it further. A replay of a recorded benchmark matches each run’s sampled requests by the arm’s name, so a renamed or swept chain does not replay a recording made under another name: record the benchmark again under the new names.

Skills

A skill is a folder of instructions for one step: a SKILL.md file with a short header and the instructions, optional text files under references/, and optional scripts under scripts/. hr_skill() reads a folder you choose. The package never looks for skills on its own and a model never chooses one: a person picks the skill and the step it goes to.

The header sits between two --- lines and is read without a YAML parser, so each line is a plain key: value. name is required, and description and version are kept. Any other key warns (hr_skill_unknown_key), and a nested or multi-line value is an error (hr_bad_skill). This skill is written into a temporary folder:

skill_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "units-skill")
dir.create(file.path(skill_dir, "references"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines(c("---",
             "name: units",
             "description: State every amount with its unit and currency.",
             "version: 1.0.0",
             "---",
             "Give every amount with its unit and its currency, as in",
             "'45.2 million dollars', never a bare number."),
           file.path(skill_dir, "SKILL.md"))
writeLines("Write 'million' in full; do not write 'M' or 'mn'.",
           file.path(skill_dir, "references", "style.md"))
units <- hr_skill(skill_dir)
units
#> <hr_skill> units version 1.0.0 (f1cdea95dadd)
#>   State every amount with its unit and currency. 
#>   instructions: 100 characters
#>   references: style.md

The skill’s text goes into the prompt as it is written. A skill from someone else can carry instructions you did not mean to send (prompt injection), so read a skill before you use it. Scripts are listed and never run; to run one, wrap it yourself in a command step, as in hr_step_command("lint", c(rscript, units$scripts[["check.R"]])).

Give a skill to a step of your own with hr_step(skill = ). Inside a chain, the step’s ctx$call() and ctx$call_json() then send the instructions and the references as a system message before the step’s own messages, and ctx$skill holds the skill. The built-in steps of gr_step() and gr_step_retrieve() build their requests in the stage they run, so they refuse a skill. The stand-in model here answers with the unit only when the skill’s instructions reach it:

units_cl <- gr_mock_client(function(messages, params) {
  skilled <- messages[[1]]$role == "system" &&
    grepl("unit and its currency", messages[[1]]$content, fixed = TRUE)
  if (skilled) "Revenue was 45.2 million dollars." else "Revenue was 45.2."
})
answer <- function(skill = NULL) {
  hr_step("answer", function(item, ctx) ctx$call(item$question)$text,
          input = "state", output = "answer", skill = skill)
}
baseline <- hr_chain(answer = answer(), name = "no-skill")
skilled <- hr_chain(answer = answer(units), name = "units-skill")
skilled$params
#> $answer.skill
#> [1] "units@f1cdea95dadd"
identical(attr(baseline, "hr_config"), attr(skilled, "hr_config"))
#> [1] FALSE

The skill’s hash covers its header, instructions, references and every byte of its scripts. It is part of the step’s fingerprint, so the two chains have different configurations, and the chain records it as the setting answer.skill, which a benchmark shows as param.answer.skill. A skill with a version gives the step that version.

To see whether the skill does what it says, compare the chain with and without it on the same questions, with a scorer that checks the rule the skill sets. This one checks that the answer names the currency:

questions <- c(q1 = "What was revenue in 2024?", q2 = "What was revenue in 2023?",
               q3 = "What was the operating cost?", q4 = "What was the order backlog?",
               q5 = "What was spent on research?", q6 = "What was the net income?")
units_ref <- hr_reference(lapply(as.list(questions), function(q) list(question = q)),
                          labels = rep("dollars", length(questions)),
                          cluster = names(questions), split = "test")
has_unit <- hr_scorer(function(item, output, label) {
  ok <- grepl(label, output, fixed = TRUE)
  list(correct = ok, outcome = if (ok) "unit" else "bare", failure_kind = NA)
}, name = "has_unit")
units_bench <- hr_benchmark(list(baseline, skilled), units_ref, runs = 5,
                            client = units_cl, scorer = has_unit)
units_report <- hr_report(units_bench, B = 200)
units_report$accuracy[, c("arm", "estimate", "lower", "upper")]
#>           arm estimate     lower     upper
#> 1    no-skill        0 0.0000000 0.3930378
#> 2 units-skill        1 0.6069622 1.0000000
units_report$contrasts[, c("arm1", "arm2", "estimate", "lower", "upper")]
#>       arm1        arm2 estimate lower      upper
#> 1 no-skill units-skill       -1    -1 0.04821512

A skill is not a setting of a step’s schema, so hr_set() cannot change it and a sweep by path cannot swap it. Sweep it with a function that builds the chain from a grid column instead:

arms <- hr_sweep(function(use_skill) {
  hr_chain(answer = answer(if (use_skill) units), name = "answer")
}, data.frame(use_skill = c(FALSE, TRUE)))
names(arms)
#> [1] "answer:use_skill=FALSE" "answer:use_skill=TRUE"
